intro_html: French onion soup gets all its magic from slow-cooked onions, and that same trick makes this chicken bowl shine. It brings a big 67 grams of protein for about $3.61 (at everyday cost), with deep, savory, oniony flavor throughout. One batch makes 14 servings, so a bag of cheap onions carries you a long way.
cost_closing_html: About $3.61 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: You get a strong 67 grams of protein and 580 calories per serving, one of the highest-protein bowls here.
upsell_html: Cheap onions, patient cooking, and a big protein payoff. That's a win any way you slice it. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: This whole dish is built on onions, so buy the big three-pound bag when it's cheap and you've got the star ingredient covered.
Greek yogurt stands in for cream here, so use plain yogurt instead of heavy cream to cut cost and add protein.
A little grated parmesan brings the salty, nutty punch, so keep a shaker of it on hand for cheap flavor across many meals.
make_it: Add the chicken, sliced onions, beef broth, and garlic powder to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours so the onions go soft, sweet, and jammy.
Shred the chicken into the pot and stir so it soaks up the broth.
Stir in the Greek yogurt off the heat for a creamy, tangy finish.
Serve over white rice and top each bowl with grated parmesan.
